source_documents.title: Contribution of radiative rate constants to crystallization-induced emission enhancement in boron-fused azobenzene complexes

reference_evidence_units.quote: it is experimentally proved that a large refractive index in an organic crystal mainly promotes the radiative processes in CIEE even without significant intermolecular electronic interactions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BAz series

reference_evidence_units.quote: This could be mainly attributed to the higher polarizability of the crystal surrounding, and implied that the molecular planarization and exciton coupling might be minor contributions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: halogenated BAz
reference_evidence_units.statement: Polarizability, not planarization or exciton coupling, explains the kr rise.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the restriction of structural relaxation in the excited state
reference_evidence_units.subject: BAz series
reference_evidence_units.statement: Crystal contacts restrict excited-state structural relaxation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the kr value of the crystalline sample of BAz-F was 1.7-fold larger than that in the solution
reference_evidence_units.subject: BAz-F
reference_evidence_units.statement: kr 1.7-fold higher in crystal, little knr change.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the slight decrease in kr,SB in a crystal was theoretically predicted due to the eﬀect of H-aggregation, especially in BAz-H and BAz-F
reference_evidence_units.subject: BAz-H, BAz-F
reference_evidence_units.statement: A weak H-aggregation effect slightly lowers kr.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: A weak H-aggregation contribution slightly opposes the kr gain.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Low-temperature comparison isolates a crystal kr acceleration attributed mainly to refractive index.
